description:
Can my dog go to this place, or which parks, beaches, trails, campgrounds or patios allow dogs: "Can I bring my dog to Point Lobos?", "state parks in Marin that allow dogs", "off-leash beaches near San Diego"?
Answers for one named place or a filtered list of one kind; each result's id names the place's full record, with every rule and source.
Inputs: query (name, city or brand; words like "cabins", "hikes", "wineries" or "dog friendly hotels in Carmel" are read as the kind and the place), type (lodging, campground incl. RV parks, cabins, beach, park, trail, restaurant, rest_area, stop; "hotel", "dog park" or "hike" are read as these), dogs_allowed, off_leash, state "CA" or "NV", county without "County", area (lake-tahoe, big-sur, east-bay), or near={lat, lon}.
Each result: yes, yes_restricted, no or varies, the rule in a sentence, verified date, URL and id. No match is an answer (outcome no_match) with did_you_mean, nearest and next. Nevada coverage is thin.

Examples:
  - "Off-leash beaches near San Diego" -> type="beach", off_leash=true, near={lat:32.72, lon:-117.16}
  - "Can I bring my dog to Point Lobos?" -> query="Point Lobos"
  - "State parks in Marin County that allow dogs" -> type="park", county="Marin", dogs_allowed=true
  - "Lake Tahoe beaches in Nevada that allow dogs" -> type="beach", state="NV", dogs_allowed=true
  - "Off-leash dog parks in Las Vegas" -> type="park", off_leash=true, county="Clark", state="NV"
  - "RV parks in Fresno County that take dogs" -> type="campground", county="Fresno", dogs_allowed=true
  - "Dog-friendly cabins in June Lake" -> type="cabins", query="June Lake", dogs_allowed=true (query="June Lake cabins" works too)
  - "Restaurants with a dog-friendly patio in Alameda" -> type="restaurant", query="Alameda"

area.description: Area id, the name a traveler gives the trip: san-francisco, east-bay, peninsula, south-bay, north-bay, lake-tahoe, big-sur, mendocino-coast, yosemite, death-valley

county.description: County name without "County", in California or Nevada, e.g. "Monterey" or "Washoe"

dogs_allowed.description: true: only places that allow dogs somewhere; false: only places that do not

near.description: Limit to places near a point; results are sorted by distance

off_leash.description: true: only places where the managing agency allows dogs off leash, at least at some times

query.description: Words to match in the name, city, county or brand

region.description: Region id, e.g. central-coast, san-diego or reno-tahoe-nevada

response_format.description: 'markdown' for readable text, 'json' for structured data

state.description: "CA" or "NV". Also tells apart counties with the same name, such as Humboldt.

type.description: Kind of place; campground covers campgrounds and RV parks (some also rent cabins), cabins covers cabin resorts with no campground, restaurant covers restaurants, cafes, bars, breweries and tasting rooms (dogs on the patio, by the owner's published policy), rest_area and stop are the roadside kinds

name: dogpolicies_search_places

accepted.description: With bad_input: each argument that could not be read, with the values it accepts

code.description: With an outcome other than ok: not_found, invalid, unavailable

did_you_mean.description: Close matches to what was asked for: towns, places, slugs or brands, best first

nearest.description: When nothing is inside the radius: the nearest places in the data, with distance_miles

next.description: Calls that would answer the question, in words

outcome.description: Absent or ok: a normal answer. no_match: nothing in the data matches, see did_you_mean, nearest and next. bad_input: the arguments cannot be used as given, see next. partial: some of the ids were found, see missing. unavailable: a live source could not be read. None of these is an error.

answer.description: The one-line answer; while a seasonal rule applies today it leads with it (see today)

citation.description: Copy-ready citation: answer, source, date checked, record URL, license

closed_now.description: Present only when Caltrans reports this rest area fully closed now. Live feed data, not a verified rule: check quickmap.dot.ca.gov

fetched_at.description: When the conditions loop read the feed

until.description: Caltrans' end time (ISO); null when no end is set

confidence.description: stated: the place's own source says it; inferred_from_agency: an agency-wide rule; inherited_brand: the chain's policy, not confirmed by this hotel

freshness.description: fresh: inside its review interval; due: past it; stale: past twice it, confirm before you go; unreadable: the last check could not read the source

today.description: Only for a place with seasonal dog rules (plover nesting season, summer beach hours): which applies on the server's date, until when, and which starts next, with the source. Repeat sentence with the answer.

date.description: The date this was computed for: the server's date

rule.description: The seasonal rule in plain words

season.description: When it runs, in the source's dates: "July 1 to May 15"

in_season.description: true: a seasonal rule is in effect on that date; null: the source gives a season without dates

rule.description: The seasonal rule in plain words

season.description: When it runs, in the source's dates: "July 1 to May 15"

sentence.description: Leads answer and citation while a seasonal rule applies or starts within 14 days; null otherwise

rule.description: The seasonal rule in plain words

season.description: When it runs, in the source's dates: "July 1 to May 15"

undated.description: Seasons the source states without dates: not known to apply

rule.description: The seasonal rule in plain words

season.description: When it runs, in the source's dates: "July 1 to May 15"

uid.description: Stable id that survives a rename

resolved_from.description: Set when a word was read as the value the tool uses: hotel as lodging, NB as north. Each key is the argument; asked is what was sent, used what it was read as

title: Search places
